newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission plans to cut scrapped-car waste.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission plans to cut scrapped-car waste.

text.p: Car makers selling into EU markets will have to make their vehicles easier to dismantle and recycle under European Commission plans to slash the mounds of car scrap and toxic waste dumped each year.

Manufacturers will have to code car parts and materials from the end of 1999 and provide wrecking yards with manuals showing how to dismantle their vehicles and remove toxic chemicals so as to cut back on a major source of dangerous waste.

Commission plans, agreed on Wednesday and due for scrutiny by EU environment ministers and the European Parliament before adoption, would set minimum recycling levels for scrapped cars at 85 percent by weight from 2005.
The figure would include an allowance for up to five percent of the wreck to be burnt with energy recovery.
The level would rise to 95 percent from 2015, with 10 percent allowed to be burnt with energy recovery.

Current practice for the eight or nine million vehicles scrapped in the EU each year leaves about one quarter as hazardous residue, about two million tonnes-worth, which is dumped in landfills where it pollutes soil and groundwater.
The Commission says some seven percent of old cars are simply abandoned, never making it to wreckers' yards.

While parts coding and manuals would go some way towards reaching the 2005 target, manufacturers will also have to design new vehicles with recycling in mind so as to meet the 2015 figure, the Commission said.
Those who don't could face the bill for eventual destruction of their vehicles if it proves impossible or too time-consuming for wreckers to dismantle them at a profit.
"This will give to producers further incentives to increase the recyclability of new vehicles," a Commission statement said.
Car wreckers' operations are also targeted by the new laws, which will require them to hold a permit to operate and to issue final owners with certificates of destruction.
Owners will need those certificates to prove that they have taken their old cars to authorised yards. Without it, they will be unable to deregister their cars from national records.
